{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Form of Transfer and Servicing Agreement

**Prepared by:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Subject:** Playbook review of the Form of Transfer and Servicing Agreement (Issuer / Depositor v. Cellco as Servicer, Marketing Agent and Custodian)

## Executive summary

This is a securitisation transfer and servicing agreement rather than a procurement or technology contract, and the risk profile is unusually favourable to us. Of the eighteen rules tested, fourteen are compliant, two require a scoping decision, one is a deviation and one is missing.

The economically significant protections all run in our direction. Ownership of the Receivables and Receivable Files vests outright in the Issuer, with delivery to the Indenture Trustee and mandated return on termination at Cellco's expense (§ II; § VII). There is no monetary limitation of liability at all, so Cellco's servicing exposure and indemnities are uncapped, while our own liability is confined by the limited-recourse provision (§ VI; § IX). Assignment is symmetrical with a full affiliate/merger carve-out for us and no change-of-control trigger for Cellco (§ X). Governing law is New York with a New York-seated, scope-limited arbitration track (§ X). There is no exclusivity, non-compete, MFN, minimum commitment, non-solicit, auto-renewal or Customer-payable liquidated damages anywhere in the document, and the transition and warranty regimes sit at or above our preferred position.

Two items warrant action. First, there is no third-party IP infringement indemnity — the Article VI indemnities are limited to Cellco's willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence, which fails both our preferred and fallback positions. Second, the Agreement contains no insurance covenant of any kind, notwithstanding that Cellco collects payments, holds Receivable Files and processes Obligor account data. Two further items (licence grant and termination for convenience) do not literally meet the playbook but should be carved out for this transaction type rather than redlined, and we set out why below.

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § II Transfer and Acquisition of Depositor Transferred Property; Representations and Warranties |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality and carve-outs | Compliant | § VI Servicer and Marketing Agent |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § X Miscellaneous |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § IX Other Agreements |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | § VIII Termination |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Needs review | § VII Servicer Resignation and Termination; Successor Servicer |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § VII Servicer Resignation and Termination; Successor Servicer |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Needs review | § VII Servicer Resignation and Termination; Successor Servicer |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § III Servicing of Receivables |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § X Miscellaneous |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | A-13 |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions | Compliant | § IV Accounts, Collections and Application of Funds |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Compliant | § VI Servicer and Marketing Agent |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Compliant | § VIII Termination |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § VII Servicer Resignation and Termination; Successor Servicer |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § III Servicing of Receivables |
| Low | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § VI Servicer and Marketing Agent |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § X Miscellaneous |

### Items requiring action

**INDEMN (deviation, § VI).** Section 6.3(a) provides Servicer and Marketing Agent indemnities with a workable notice and defence-control procedure, but the trigger reaches only willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence and there is no third-party IP infringement indemnity anywhere in the document. That fails our fallback as well as our preferred position. We propose inserting a concise IP infringement indemnity as new Section 6.3(a)(iii), with the customary Issuer-modification, combination and specification exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies and a 3x annual fees super-cap, leaving the existing Proceedings procedure, survival and repayment mechanics untouched. We are targeting the fallback rather than the preferred position because the existing indemnitee set (the Owner Trustee, Indenture Trustee and their officers, directors, employees and agents) extends beyond Customer and affiliates; the absence of an indemnitee cooperation duty is a negotiation point rather than a redline.

**INSURANCE (missing, § X).** There is no insurance covenant of any kind. The only references to insurance are Obligor premiums billed to wireless accounts and FDIC deposit insurance in the "Qualified Institution" definition. Cellco collects payments, holds Receivable Files and processes Obligor account data, and the Section 6.3(a) indemnity provides no insured capacity. We propose a short covenant at our preferred limits as new Section 10.14 (CGL, E&O, cyber and workers' compensation, with certificates), without the self-insurance permission, post-termination tail or "at its own expense" wording.

### Items requiring a scoping decision

**LICENSE (needs review, § VII).** Cellco supplies us with no licensed product, software or deliverable, and there is no affirmative licence grant in the document to test — all "grant" usages are security-interest grants and all other "licence" usages are regulatory due-qualification representations. Inserting a licence grant would not fit the transaction structure. Section 7.5(b), which negates any obligation to license Cellco's processes, models or servicing software to a Successor Servicer, is the same commercial term addressed under TRANSITION and is not redlined twice.

**T4C (needs review, § VII).** Cellco's side exceeds our preferred position: Section 7.1 bars resignation except where it is legally unable to perform, Section 7.3 compels continued performance until a Successor Servicer accepts, Section 7.5 imposes cooperation and transition costs on Cellco, and Section 7.4(a)(ii) makes the Indenture Trustee automatic backstop servicer. On our side there is no convenience right — removal requires a Servicer Termination Event and is exercised by the Indenture Trustee at the Controlling Class's direction — and the term runs until the last Receivable is paid. Read literally that is a walk-away trigger, but the underlying harm is absent (fees accrue per Collection Period, with no prepaid fees, minimum commitment or early-termination fee), and a convenience right would be exercised through the Administrator, which is Cellco itself. We recommend a documented carve-out rather than a redline.

## Walk-away items

1. **Uninsured provider handling our data (INSURANCE, § X).** The complete absence of an insurance covenant, in circumstances where Cellco collects payments, holds Receivable Files and processes Obligor account data, is walk-away territory under the playbook. We treat this as a required insertion, not a negotiable preference.
2. **No Customer termination for convenience in a multi-year term (T4C, § VII).** This literally engages the walk-away trigger and is recorded as such, but we do not recommend acting on it: the fee structure creates no prepayment or minimum-commitment exposure, and the removal architecture is standard bankruptcy-remote SPE and rating-agency structure. We seek an approved carve-out instead.

For completeness, the walk-away triggers under IP (assignment of our rights, joint ownership) and LOL-CAP (Vendor-only cap, sub-six-month cap, indemnities inside a cap) are expressly absent; there is no cap of any kind, and we should not propose one.

## Next steps

1. Issue the two redlines to counsel for Cellco: the IP infringement indemnity at Section 6.3(a)(iii) and the insurance covenant at new Section 10.14, each with a short "[Playbook]" rationale citing the fallback and preferred positions respectively.
2. Obtain a documented playbook carve-out for securitisation transfer-and-servicing agreements covering LICENSE and T4C; if the deal team wants a servicing-removal lever, pursue it as an Indenture/Controlling-Class direction right rather than an Issuer convenience termination.
3. Confirm with the deal team that we should not introduce a monetary liability cap, given that Cellco's servicing exposure and indemnities are presently uncapped.
4. Note for the file, without redline: our Section 3.6 access to Cellco's records is once per calendar year, must be exercised simultaneously by all parties at Cellco's offices, and is subject to Cellco's own security, confidentiality, privacy and data-protection policies; the Section 7.5(b) delivery obligation is "as soon as practicable" with no fixed format or deletion certification; and residual assignment consent under Section 10.2(a) is absolute rather than subject to a reasonableness standard. Each is a sub-preferred mechanic, not a material failure, and should be raised in negotiation only if the counterparty reopens the relevant article.
5. Resist any future addition of exclusivity, field-of-use, non-compete, MFN, minimum-commitment or renewal-and-uplift constructs, all of which are currently absent and none of which is necessary given the Issuer's and Depositor's narrowly circumscribed permitted activities."}
